{"parentUuid":"a64e1e34-1e87-4f7f-b3d1-bf5c7c76e31f","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011CfYBL2Rkt4jiG8GUYXehU","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_016AFkRuzgfnXh7WCqcZEeWy","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/Users/davelleat/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/tests/test_t11_report_chart_images.py","content":"\"\"\"T11: Chart images on Reports (issue #13).\n\nThe checks on an upload itself (formats, size, count, names) are T10's shared\ncode, tested there; here, what a Report adds: the lockdown, the Report's\npages and export, and independence from its attached PDF.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport re\n\nimport pytest\nfrom fastapi.testclient import TestClient\n\nfrom app import settings\nfrom app.publish import render_site\nfrom tests.conftest import post_form, second_analyst\nfrom tests.test_t04_reports import REPORT, create_report\nfrom tests.test_t05_report_files import PDF, pdf, post_with_file, reports_file\nfrom tests.test_t07_public_site import crawl, published_bite, published_report\nfrom tests.test_t08_publish import exported\nfrom tests.test_t09_tables import content_body\nfrom tests.test_t10_chart_images import CHART, WEBP, img_tags, png, png_bytes, preview_div\n\nPNG = png()[1]\n\n\ndef upload(c: TestClient, rid: str, file, *, with_csrf=True):\n    return post_with_file(c, f\"/admin/reports/{rid}/images\", {}, file, with_csrf=with_csrf)\n\n\ndef delete_image(c: TestClient, rid: str, name: str, *, with_csrf=True):\n    return post_form(c, f\"/admin/reports/{rid}/images/{name}/delete\", {}, with_csrf=with_csrf)\n\n\ndef stored(rid: str) -> list[str]:\n    folder = settings.UPLOADS / \"images\" / \"reports\" / rid\n    return sorted(p.name for p in folder.iterdir()) if folder.exists() else []\n\n\ndef publish(director: TestClient, rid: str) -> None:\n    assert post_form(director, f\"/admin/reports/{rid}/publish\", {}).status_code == 303\n\n\ndef edit_report(c: TestClient, rid: str, file=None, **override):\n    return post_with_file(c, f\"/admin/reports/{rid}\", {**REPORT, **override}, file)\n\n\n# Who may add or delete a Report's images\n\ndef test_analyst_uploads_to_a_draft_report_and_the_edit_page_lists_it(client_as):\n    analyst = client_as(\"editor\")\n    rid = create_report(analyst)\n\n    response = upload(analyst, rid, png())\n    assert response.status_code == 303\n    assert response.headers[\"location\"] == f\"/admin/reports/{rid}\"\n    assert \"![Description](image:fall-by-class.png)\" in analyst.get(f\"/admin/reports/{rid}\").text\n    assert stored(rid) == [\"fall-by-class.png\"]\n\n    served = analyst.get(f\"/admin/reports/{rid}/images/fall-by-class.png\")\n    assert served.status_code == 200 and served.content == PNG\n    assert served.headers[\"content-type\"] == \"image/png\"\n    assert served.headers[\"x-content-type-options\"] == \"nosniff\"\n\n\ndef test_any_analyst_manages_images_on_a_draft_report_another_analyst_started(client_as):\n    director = client_as(\"admin\")\n    riley = second_analyst(director)\n    rid = create_report(client_as(\"editor\"))\n\n    assert upload(riley, rid, png(\"riley.png\")).status_code == 303\n    assert upload(riley, rid, png(\"drop.png\")).status_code == 303\n    assert delete_image(riley, rid, \"drop.png\").status_code == 303\n    assert stored(rid) == [\"riley.png\"]\n\n\ndef test_the_director_manages_images_on_a_report_in_any_state(client_as):\n    director = client_as(\"admin\")\n    draft = create_report(client_as(\"editor\"))\n    published = published_report(director, slug=\"cds\")\n\n    for rid in (draft, published):\n        assert upload(director, rid, png(\"keep.png\")).status_code == 303\n        assert upload(director, rid, png(\"drop.png\")).status_code == 303\n        assert delete_image(director, rid, \"drop.png\").status_code == 303\n        assert stored(rid) == [\"keep.png\"], rid\n\n\ndef test_once_published_an_analysts_upload_and_delete_are_rejected(client_as):\n    director, analyst = client_as(\"admin\"), client_as(\"editor\")\n    rid = create_report(analyst)\n    # Allowed while the Report is a draft...\n    assert upload(analyst, rid, png(\"before.png\")).status_code == 303\n    assert upload(analyst, rid, png(\"also.png\")).status_code == 303\n    assert delete_image(analyst, rid, \"also.png\").status_code == 303\n\n    publish(director, rid)\n    # ...and rejected server-side once it is published, whatever is sent.\n    assert upload(analyst, rid, png(\"after.png\")).status_code == 403\n    assert upload(analyst, rid, png(\"before.png\", png_bytes(b\"\\x00\\x00\\xff\"))).status_code == 403\n    assert upload(analyst, rid, (\"chart.svg\", b\"<svg/>\", \"image/svg+xml\")).status_code == 403\n    assert delete_image(analyst, rid, \"before.png\").status_code == 403\n    assert delete_image(analyst, rid, \"no-such.png\").status_code == 403\n    assert stored(rid) == [\"before.png\"]\n    assert analyst.get(f\"/admin/reports/{rid}/images/before.png\").content == PNG\n\n    # Unpublished again, it is the Analyst's to change once more.\n    assert post_form(director, f\"/admin/reports/{rid}/unpublish\", {}).status_code == 303\n    assert delete_image(analyst, rid, \"before.png\").status_code == 303\n\n\ndef test_a_locked_report_shows_its_images_but_no_image_forms(client_as):\n    director, analyst = client_as(\"admin\"), client_as(\"editor\")\n    rid = create_report(analyst, body=CHART)\n    upload(analyst, rid, png())\n    publish(director, rid)\n\n    page = analyst.get(f\"/admin/reports/{rid}\").text\n    assert img_tags(preview_div(page)) == [\n        f'<img src=\"/admin/reports/{rid}/images/fall-by-class.png\" alt=\"Fall enrollment by class\">']\n    assert f'action=\"/admin/reports/{rid}/images' not in page\n    assert f'action=\"/admin/reports/{rid}/images' in director.get(f\"/admin/reports/{rid}\").text\n\n\ndef test_upload_checks_are_t10s(client_as):\n    analyst = client_as(\"editor\")\n    rid = create_report(analyst)\n    for file, message in [((\"chart.svg\", b\"<svg/>\", \"image/svg+xml\"), \"Only PNG, JPEG, or WebP\"),\n                          (png(content=b\"<html></html>\"), \"not a valid PNG\"),\n                          ((\"\", b\"\", \"application/octet-stream\"), \"Choose an image\")]:\n        response = upload(analyst, rid, file)\n        assert response.status_code == 400 and message in response.text, file\n    for i in range(10):\n        upload(analyst, rid, png(f\"chart-{i}.png\"))\n    response = upload(analyst, rid, png(\"chart-10.png\"))\n    assert response.status_code == 400 and \"This Report already has 10 images\" in response.text\n    assert len(stored(rid)) == 10\n\n\ndef test_image_routes_404_for_a_missing_report_or_image(client_as):\n    director = client_as(\"admin\")\n    rid = create_report(director)\n    upload(director, rid, png())\n    assert upload(director, \"9999\", png()).status_code == 404\n    assert delete_image(director, \"9999\", \"fall-by-class.png\").status_code == 404\n    assert director.get(\"/admin/reports/9999/images/fall-by-class.png\").status_code == 404\n    assert post_form(director, \"/admin/reports/9999/preview\", {\"body\": CHART}).status_code == 404\n    for name in (\"..%2F..%2Fcms.db\", \"FALL-BY-CLASS.png\", \"no-such.png\"):\n        assert director.get(f\"/admin/reports/{rid}/images/{name}\").status_code == 404, name\n        assert delete_image(director, rid, name).status_code == 404, name\n    assert stored(rid) == [\"fall-by-class.png\"]\n\n\ndef test_deleting_a_report_deletes_its_images_and_its_file(client_as):\n    director = client_as(\"admin\")\n    rid = create_report(director)\n    assert edit_report(director, rid, pdf()).status_code == 303\n    upload(director, rid, png())\n\n    assert post_form(director, f\"/admin/reports/{rid}/delete\", {}).status_code == 303\n    assert not (settings.UPLOADS / \"images\" / \"reports\" / rid).exists()\n    assert not reports_file(rid).exists()\n\n\ndef test_a_new_report_never_inherits_images_left_under_its_id(client_as, client):\n    director = client_as(\"admin\")\n    first = create_report(director)\n    leftover = settings.UPLOADS / \"images\" / \"reports\" / str(int(first) + 1)\n    leftover.mkdir(parents=True)\n    (leftover / \"old-chart.png\").write_bytes(PNG)\n\n    rid = published_report(director, slug=\"cds\", body=\"![Old](image:old-chart.png)\")\n    assert rid == str(int(first) + 1)\n    assert stored(rid) == []\n    assert client.get(\"/images/reports/cds/old-chart.png\").status_code == 404\n\n\n# The chart images and the attached PDF are independent\n\ndef test_images_and_the_attached_pdf_leave_each_other_untouched(client_as):\n    analyst = client_as(\"editor\")\n    rid = create_report(analyst)\n    assert edit_report(analyst, rid, pdf()).status_code == 303\n\n    # Adding and removing an image leaves the PDF.\n    upload(analyst, rid, png(\"keep.png\"))\n    upload(analyst, rid, png(\"drop.png\"))\n    delete_image(analyst, rid, \"drop.png\")\n    assert reports_file(rid).read_bytes() == PDF\n    assert \"factbook-2026.pdf\" in analyst.get(f\"/admin/reports/{rid}\").text\n\n    # Replacing, then removing, the PDF leaves the images.\n    revised = PDF.replace(b\"%%EOF\", b\"% revised\\n%%EOF\")\n    assert edit_report(analyst, rid, pdf(\"factbook-2027.pdf\", revised)).status_code == 303\n    assert reports_file(rid).read_bytes() == revised\n    assert stored(rid) == [\"keep.png\"]\n    assert post_form(analyst, f\"/admin/reports/{rid}/file/delete\", {}).status_code == 303\n    assert not reports_file(rid).exists()\n    assert stored(rid) == [\"keep.png\"]\n    # Saving the body with no file chosen leaves both.\n    assert edit_report(analyst, rid, body=CHART).status_code == 303\n    assert stored(rid) == [\"keep.png\"]\n\n\ndef test_a_pdf_named_like_an_image_is_not_one_and_vice_versa(client_as):\n    analyst = client_as(\"editor\")\n    rid = create_report(analyst)\n    assert upload(analyst, rid, (\"factbook.pdf\", PDF, \"application/pdf\")).status_code == 400\n    assert edit_report(analyst, rid, (\"chart.png\", PNG, \"image/png\")).status_code == 400\n    assert stored(rid) == [] and not reports_file(rid).exists()\n\n\n# Login and CSRF\n\ndef test_every_report_image_route_requires_login(client_as, client):\n    director = client_as(\"admin\")\n    rid = create_report(director)\n    upload(director, rid, png())\n\n    for method, path in [(\"get\", f\"/admin/reports/{rid}/images/fall-by-class.png\"),\n                         (\"post\", f\"/admin/reports/{rid}/images\"),\n                         (\"post\", f\"/admin/reports/{rid}/images/fall-by-class.png/delete\"),\n                         (\"post\", f\"/admin/reports/{rid}/preview\")]:\n        response = getattr(client, method)(path, follow_redirects=False)\n        assert response.status_code == 303 and response.headers[\"location\"] == \"/login\", path\n    assert stored(rid) == [\"fall-by-class.png\"]\n\n\ndef test_report_image_forms_carry_csrf_and_a_stripped_post_is_rejected(client_as):\n    director = client_as(\"admin\")\n    rid = create_report(director)\n    upload(director, rid, png())\n\n    page = director.get(f\"/admin/reports/{rid}\").text\n    for action in (f\"/admin/reports/{rid}/images\", f\"/admin/reports/{rid}/images/fall-by-class.png/delete\"):\n        form = re.search(rf'<form[^>]*action=\"{re.escape(action)}\".*?</form>', page, re.S)\n        assert form and 'name=\"csrf_token\"' in form.group(0), action\n\n    assert upload(director, rid, png(\"other.png\"), with_csrf=False).status_code == 403\n    assert delete_image(director, rid, \"fall-by-class.png\", with_csrf=False).status_code == 403\n    assert stored(rid) == [\"fall-by-class.png\"]\n\n\n# The image: reference, as for a Data Bite\n\ndef test_the_preview_shows_the_image_from_the_admin_console(client_as):\n    analyst = client_as(\"editor\")\n    rid = create_report(analyst, body=CHART)\n    upload(analyst, rid, png())\n\n    expected = f'<img src=\"/admin/reports/{rid}/images/fall-by-class.png\" alt=\"Fall enrollment by class\">'\n    preview = post_form(analyst, f\"/admin/reports/{rid}/preview\", {\"body\": CHART})\n    assert preview.status_code == 200 and img_tags(preview.text) == [expected]\n    page = analyst.get(f\"/admin/reports/{rid}\").text\n    assert img_tags(preview_div(page)) == [expected]\n    assert f'\"/admin/reports/{rid}/preview\"' in page\n\n\ndef test_the_public_page_and_the_export_show_the_image_relatively(client_as, client, tmp_path):\n    director = client_as(\"admin\")\n    rid = published_report(director, body=CHART)\n    upload(director, rid, png())\n\n    expected = '<img src=\"../images/reports/factbook/fall-by-class.png\" alt=\"Fall enrollment by class\">'\n    assert img_tags(content_body(client.get(\"/reports/factbook.html\").text)) == [expected]\n    served = client.get(\"/images/reports/factbook/fall-by-class.png\")\n    assert served.status_code == 200 and served.content == PNG\n    assert served.headers[\"content-type\"] == \"image/png\"\n    assert served.headers[\"x-content-type-options\"] == \"nosniff\"\n\n    site = exported(render_site(tmp_path / \"site\"))\n    assert img_tags(site[\"reports/factbook.html\"].decode()) == [expected]\n    assert site[\"images/reports/factbook/fall-by-class.png\"] == PNG\n\n\ndef test_an_unknown_name_renders_nothing(client_as, client):\n    director = client_as(\"admin\")\n    body = \"Before ![Missing chart](image:no-such.png) after\"\n    rid = published_report(director, in html, html\n        assert \"Before\" in html and \"after\" in html\n\n\ndef test_script_in_the_description_is_inert(client_as, client):\n    director = client_as(\"admin\")\n    body = '![x\" onerror=\"alert(1)](image:fall-by-class.png) ![<script>alert(1)</script>](image:fall-by-class.png)'\n    rid = published_report(director, body=body)\n    upload(director, rid, png())\n\n    html = test_the_edit_page_warns_of_an_empty_description_without_blocking_the_save(client_as):\n    analyst = client_as(\"editor\")\n    rid = create_report(analyst)\n    upload(analyst, rid, png())\n\n    assert edit_report(analyst, rid, body=\"![](image:fall-by-class.png)\").status_code == 303\n    warning = re.search(r'<p class=\"content-image-warning\"[^>]*>(.*?)</p>',\n test_a_draft_reports_images_are_never_public(client_as, client, tmp_path):\n    director, analyst = client_as(\"admin\"), client_as(\"editor\")\n    published_report(director)\n    draft = upload(director, rid, png())\n    assert edit_report(director, rid, slug=\"factbook-2026\", body=CHART).status_code == 303\n\n    assert return post_with_file(c, f\"/admin/reports/{rid}/images\", {}, file, with_csrf=with_csrf)\n\n\ndef delete_image(c: TestClient, rid: str, name: str, *, with_csrf=True):\n    return post_form(c, sorted(p.name for p in folder.iterdir()) if folder.exists() else []\n\n\ndef publish(director: TestClient, rid: str) -> None:\n    assert post_form(director, f\"/admin/reports/{rid}/publish\", {}).status_code == 303\n\n\ndef edit_report(c: TestClient, rid: str, file=None, **override):\n    return post_with_file(c, f\"/admin/reports/{rid}\", {**REPORT, **override}, file)\n\n\n# Who may add = upload(analyst, rid, png())\n    assert response.status_code == 303\n    assert response.headers[\"location\"] == f\"/admin/reports/{rid}\"\n    assert \"![Description](image:fall-by-class.png)\" in analyst.get(f\"/admin/reports/{rid}\").text\n    assert stored(rid) == [\"fall-by-class.png\"]\n\n    served = analyst.get(f\"/admin/reports/{rid}/images/fall-by-class.png\")\n    assert served.status_code == 200 and served.content == PNG\n    assert served.headers[\"content-type\"] == \"image/png\"\n    assert served.headers[\"x-content-type-options\"] == \"nosniff\"\n\n\ndef test_any_analyst_manages_images_on_a_draft_report_another_analyst_started(client_as):\n    director = client_as(\"admin\")\n    riley = second_analyst(director)\n    rid = create_report(client_as(\"editor\"))\n\n    assert upload(riley, rid, png(\"riley.png\")).status_code == 303\n    assert upload(riley, rid, png(\"drop.png\")).status_code == 303\n    assert delete_image(riley, rid, \"drop.png\").status_code == 303\n    assert stored(rid) == [\"riley.png\"]\n\n\ndef test_the_director_manages_images_on_a_report_in_any_state(client_as):\n    director = client_as(\"admin\")\n    draft = create_report(client_as(\"editor\"))\n    published = published_report(director, slug=\"cds\")\n\n    for rid in (draft, published):\n        assert upload(director, rid, png(\"keep.png\")).status_code == 303\n        assert upload(director, rid, png(\"drop.png\")).status_code == 303\n        assert delete_image(director, rid, \"drop.png\").status_code == 303\n        assert stored(rid) == [\"keep.png\"], rid\n\n\ndef test_once_published_an_analysts_upload_and_delete_are_rejected(client_as):\n    director, analyst = client_as(\"admin\"), client_as(\"editor\")\n    rid = create_report(analyst)\n    # Allowed while the Report is a draft...\n    assert upload(analyst, rid, png(\"before.png\")).status_code == 303\n    assert upload(analyst, rid, png(\"also.png\")).status_code == 303\n    assert delete_image(analyst, rid, \"also.png\").status_code == 303\n\n    publish(director, rid)\n    # ...and rejected server-side once it is published, whatever is sent.\n    assert upload(analyst, rid, png(\"after.png\")).status_code == 403\n    assert upload(analyst, rid, png(\"before.png\", png_bytes(b\"\\x00\\x00\\xff\"))).status_code == 403\n    assert upload(analyst, rid, (\"chart.svg\", b\"<svg/>\", \"image/svg+xml\")).status_code == 403\n    assert delete_image(analyst, rid, \"before.png\").status_code == 403\n    assert delete_image(analyst, rid, \"no-such.png\").status_code == 403\n    assert stored(rid) == [\"before.png\"]\n    assert analyst.get(f\"/admin/reports/{rid}/images/before.png\").content == PNG\n\n    # Unpublished again, it is the Analyst's to change once more.\n    assert post_form(director, f\"/admin/reports/{rid}/unpublish\", {}).status_code == 303\n    assert delete_image(analyst, rid, \"before.png\").status_code == 303\n\n\ndef test_a_locked_report_shows_its_images_but_no_image_forms(client_as):\n    director, analyst = client_as(\"admin\"), client_as(\"editor\")\n    rid = f'action=\"/admin/reports/{rid}/images' in director.get(f\"/admin/reports/{rid}\").text\n\n\ndef test_upload_checks_are_t10s(client_as):\n    analyst = client_as(\"editor\")\n    rid = valid PNG\"),\n                          ((\"\", b\"\", \"application/octet-stream\"), \"Choose an image\")]:\n        response = upload(analyst, rid, file)\n        assert response.status_code == 400 and message in response.text, file\n    for i in range(10):\n        upload(analyst, rid, png(f\"chart-{i}.png\"))\n    response = upload(analyst, rid, png(\"chart-10.png\"))\n    assert response.status_code == 400 and \"This Report already has 10 images\" in response.text\n    assert len(stored(rid)) == 10\n\n\ndef test_image_routes_404_for_a_missing_report_or_image(client_as):\n [\"fall-by-class.png\"]\n\n\ndef test_deleting_a_report_deletes_its_images_and_its_file(client_as):\n    director = client_as(\"admin\")\n    rid = create_report(director)\n    assert Who may do what is decided by each type's own\nmodule and routes, not here.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport re\nimport sqlite3\nfrom collections.abc import Callable\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\n\nfrom app import db\n\nSTATUS_LABELS = {\"draft\": \"Draft\", \"published\": \"Published\"}\n# Runs inside the transaction that wrote an item's row, given the connection and\n# the item's id; if it raises, the row's change is rolled back with it.\nAlsoWrite = Callable[[sqlite3.Connection, int], None]\n_SLUG_PATTERN = re.compile(r\"[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*\")\n# A slug names its item's page, <type folder>/<slug>.html, on the public site;\n# <type folder>/index.html is taken by the type's list page.\n_RESERVED_SLUGS = {\"index\"}\n\n\nclass ContentError(ValueError):\n    \"\"\"Content broke a rule; the message is safe to show.\"\"\"\n\n\nclass DuplicateSlug(ContentError):\n    pass\n\n\ndef validate(title: str, slug: str, body: str) -> tuple[str, str, str]:\n    title, slug = title.strip(), slug.strip()\n    if not title:\n        raise ContentError(\"Enter a title.\")\n    if not _SLUG_PATTERN.fullmatch(slug):\n        raise ContentError(\"Slugs use lowercase letters, digits, and single \"\n                           \"hyphens, e.g. fall-enrollment.\")\n    if slug in _RESERVED_SLUGS:\n        raise ContentError(f\"The slug {slug} is reserved for the list page; \"\n                           \"choose another.\")\n    if not body.strip():\n        raise ContentError(\"Enter a body.\")\n    return title, slug, body\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass ContentTable:\n    \"\"\"One content type's table. `table` is a fixed identifier from this\n    codebase, never user input.\"\"\"\n    table: str  # e.g. \"reports\"\n    noun: str   # e.g. \"Report\", for messages\n\n    def _select(self, where: str, order: str, params: tuple = ()) -> list[sqlite3.Row]:\n        with db.connect() as conn:\n            return conn.execute(\n                f\"SELECT c.*, u.name AS author_name FROM {self.table} c\"\n                f\" JOIN users u ON u.id = c.author_id WHERE {where} ORDER BY {order}\",\n                params,\n            ).fetchall()\n\n    def _duplicate_slug_error(self, exc: sqlite3.IntegrityError, slug: str) -> DuplicateSlug:\n        \"\"\"Translate the slug's UNIQUE violation; re-raise any other constraint.\"\"\"\n        if f\"{self.table}.slug\" not in str(exc):\n            raise exc\n        return DuplicateSlug(f\"Another {self.noun} already uses the slug {slug}.\")\n\n    def create(self, title: str, slug: str, body: str, author_id: int, *,\n               also: AlsoWrite | None = None) -> int:\n        \"\"\"Create a draft.\"\"\"\n        title, slug, body = validate(title, slug, body)\n        try:\n            with db.connect() as conn:\n                item_id = conn.execute(\n                    f\"INSERT INTO {self.table} (title, slug, body, author_id)\"\n                    \" VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)\",\n                    (title, slug, body, author_id),\n                ).lastrowid\n                if also:\n                    also(conn, item_id)\n        except sqlite3.IntegrityError as exc:\n            raise self._duplicate_slug_error(exc, slug) from None\n        return item_id\n\n    def update(self, item_id: int, title: str, slug: str, body: str, *,\n               drafts_only: bool = False, also: AlsoWrite | None = None) -> bool:\n        \"\"\"Edit title, slug, and body. The author, created_at, and status are\n        kept. With drafts_only, a published item is left alone. False if\n        nothing was changed.\"\"\"\n        title, slug, body = validate(title, slug, body)\n        try:\n            with db.connect() as conn:\n                changed = conn.execute(\n                    f\"UPDATE {self.table} SET title = ?, slug = ?, body = ?,\"\n                    \" updated_at = datetime('now')\"\n                    \" WHERE id = ? AND (status = 'draft' OR NOT ?)\",\n                    (title, slug, body, item_id, drafts_only),\n                ).rowcount == 1\n                if changed and also:\n                    also(conn, item_id)\n                return changed\n        except sqlite3.IntegrityError as exc:\n            raise self._duplicate_slug_error(exc, slug) from None\n\n    def touch(self, item_id: int, *, also: AlsoWrite | None = None) -> bool:\n        \"\"\"Mark the item as changed now, for a change outside its row (e.g.\n        its images), made by `also` in the same transaction. False if there is\n        no such item.\"\"\"\n        with db.connect() as conn:\n            changed = conn.execute(\n                f\"UPDATE {self.table} SET updated_at = datetime('now') WHERE id = ?\",\n                (item_id,),\n            ).rowcount == 1\n            if changed and also:\n                also(conn, item_id)\n            return changed\n\n    def get(self, item_id: int) -> sqlite3.Row | None:\n        rows = self._select(\"c.id = ?\", \"c.id\", (item_id,))\n        return rows[0] if rows else None\n\n    def list_all(self, status: str | None = None) -> list[sqlite3.Row]:\n        \"\"\"Every item, or only those in `status`; most recently updated first.\"\"\"\n        where, params = (\"1\", ()) if status is None else (\"c.status = ?\", (status,))\n        return self._select(where, \"c.updated_at DESC, c.id DESC\", params)\n\n    def count_by_status(self) -> dict[str, int]:\n        \"\"\"How many items are in each status, zero included, e.g.\n        {\"draft\": 2, \"published\": 0}.\"\"\"\n        with db.connect() as conn:\n            rows = conn.execute(\n                f\"SELECT status, COUNT(*) FROM {self.table} GROUP BY status\").fetchall()\n        return {**dict.fromkeys(STATUS_LABELS, 0), **dict(rows)}\n\n    def list_published(self, order: str) -> list[sqlite3.Row]:\n        return self._select(\"c.status = 'published'\", order)\n\n    def get_published(self, slug: str) -> sqlite3.Row | None:\n        \"\"\"The published item with this slug; None for a draft or no such item.\"\"\"\n        rows = self._select(\"c.status = 'published' AND c.slug = ?\", \"c.id\", (slug,))\n        return rows[0] if rows else None\n\n    def set_status(self, item_id: int, status: str) -> bool:\n        \"\"\"Publish or unpublish. False if there is no such item.\"\"\"\n        with db.connect() as conn:\n            return conn.execute(\n                f\"UPDATE {self.table} SET status = ?, updated_at = datetime('now')\"\n                \" WHERE id = ?\",\n                (status, item_id),\n            ).rowcount == 1\n\n    def delete(self, item_id: int) -> bool:\n        \"\"\"False if there is no such item.\"\"\"\n        with db.connect() as conn:\n            return conn.execute(\n                f\"DELETE FROM {self.table} WHERE id = ?\", (item_id,)).rowcount == 1\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":106,"oldLines":14,"newStart":106,"newLines":17,"lines":["         except sqlite3.IntegrityError as exc:","             raise self._duplicate_slug_error(exc, slug) from None"," ","-    def touch(self, item_id: int, *, also: AlsoWrite | None = None) -> bool:","+    def touch(self, item_id: int, *, drafts_only: bool = False,","+              also: AlsoWrite | None = None) -> bool:","         \"\"\"Mark the item as changed now, for a change outside its row (e.g.","-        its images), made by `also` in the same transaction. {"parentUuid":"00598da5-64e3-4e41-92d5-e723ef1f43f7","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"2aef766b-ab88-4630-8ee5-e3473f8fa18d","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Base directory for this skill: /Users/davelleat/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-plugins-official/mattpocock-skills/1.2.3/skills/engineering/code-review\n\nTwo-axis review of the diff between `HEAD` and a fixed point the user supplies:\n\n- **Standards**: does the code conform to this repo's documented coding standards?\n- **Spec**: does the code faithfully implement the originating issue / spec?\n\nBoth axes run as **parallel sub-agents** so they don't pollute each other's context, then this skill aggregates their findings.\n\nThe issue tracker should have been provided to you. If `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md` is missing, tell the user to run `/setup-matt-pocock-skills`.\n\n## Process\n\n### 1. Pin the fixed point\n\nWhatever the user said is the fixed point (a commit SHA, branch name, tag, `main`, `HEAD~5`, etc.). If they didn't specify one, ask for it.\n\nCapture the diff command once: `git diff <fixed-point>...HEAD` (three-dot, so the comparison is against the merge-base). Also note the list of commits via `git log <fixed-point>..HEAD --oneline`.\n\nBefore going further, confirm the fixed point resolves (`git rev-parse <fixed-point>`) and the diff is non-empty. A bad ref or empty diff should fail here, not inside two parallel sub-agents.\n\n### 2. Identify the spec source\n\nLook for the originating spec, in this order:\n\n1. Issue references in the commit messages (`#123`, `Closes #45`, GitLab `!67`, etc.), fetched via the workflow in `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`.\n2. A path the user passed as an argument.\n3. A spec file under `docs/`, `specs/`, or `.scratch/` matching the branch name or feature.\n4. If nothing is found, ask the user where the spec is. If they say there isn't one, the **Spec** sub-agent will skip and report \"no spec available\".\n\n### 3. Identify the standards sources\n\nAnything in the repo that documents how code should be written, such as `CODING_STANDARDS.md` or `CONTRIBUTING.md`.\n\nOn top of whatever the repo documents, the Standards axis always carries the **smell baseline** below: a fixed set of Fowler code smells (_Refactoring_, ch.3) that applies even when a repo documents nothing. Two rules bind it:\n\n- **The repo overrides.** A documented repo standard always wins; where it endorses something the baseline would flag, suppress the smell.\n- **Always a judgement call.** Each smell is a labelled heuristic (\"possible Feature Envy\"), never a hard violation. Like any standard here, skip anything tooling already enforces.\n\nEach smell reads *what it is* → *how to fix*; match it against the diff:\n\n- **Mysterious Name**: a function, variable, or type whose name doesn't reveal what it does or holds. → rename it; if no honest name comes, the design's murky.\n- **Duplicated Code**: the same logic shape appears in more than one hunk or file in the change. → extract the shared shape, call it from both.\n- **Feature Envy**: a method that reaches into another object's data more than its own. → move the method onto the data it envies.\n- **Data Clumps**: the same few fields or params keep travelling together (a type wanting to be born). → bundle them into one type, pass that.\n- **Primitive Obsession**: a primitive or string standing in for a domain concept that deserves its own type. → give the concept its own small type.\n- **Repeated Switches**: the same `switch`/`if`-cascade on the same type recurs across the change. → replace with polymorphism, or one map both sites share.\n- **Shotgun Surgery**: one logical change forces scattered edits across many files in the diff. → gather what changes together into one module.\n- **Divergent Change**: one file or module is edited for several unrelated reasons. → split so each module changes for one reason.\n- **Speculative Generality**: abstraction, parameters, or hooks added for needs the spec doesn't have. → delete it; inline back until a real need shows.\n- **Message Chains**: long `a.b().c().d()` navigation the caller shouldn't depend on. → hide the walk behind one method on the first object.\n- **Middle Man**: a class or function that mostly just delegates onward. → cut it, call the real target direct.\n- **Refused Bequest**: a subclass or implementer that ignores or overrides most of what it inherits. → drop the inheritance, use composition.\n\n### 4. Spawn both sub-agents in parallel\n\n**Standards sub-agent prompt** should include:\n\n- The full diff command and commit list.\n- The list of standards-source files you found in step 3, **plus the smell baseline from step 3** pasted in full (the sub-agent has no other access to it).\n- The brief: \"Report, per file/hunk where relevant, (a) every place the diff violates a documented standard: cite the standard (file + the rule); and (b) any baseline smell you spot: name it and quote the hunk. Distinguish hard violations from judgement calls: documented-standard breaches can be hard, but baseline smells are always judgement calls, and a documented repo standard overrides the baseline. Skip anything tooling enforces. Under 400 words.\"\n\n**Spec sub-agent prompt** should include:\n\n- The diff command and commit list.\n- The path or fetched contents of the spec.\n- The brief: \"Report: (a) requirements the spec asked for that are missing or partial; (b) behaviour in the diff that wasn't asked for (scope creep); (c) requirements that look implemented but where the implementation looks wrong. Quote the spec line for each finding. Under 400 words.\"\n\nIf the spec is missing, skip the Spec sub-agent and note this in the final report.\n\n### 5. Aggregate\n\nPresent the two reports under `## Standards` and `## Spec` headings, verbatim or lightly cleaned. Do **not** merge or rerank findings, because the two axes are deliberately separate (see _Why two axes_).\n\nEnd with a one-line summary: total findings per axis, and the worst issue _within each axis_ (if any). Don't pick a single winner across axes: that's the reranking the separation exists to prevent.\n\n## Why two axes\n\nA change can pass one axis and fail the other:\n\n- Code that follows every standard but implements the wrong thing → **Standards pass, Spec fail.**\n- Code that does exactly what the issue asked but breaks the project's conventions → **Spec pass, Standards fail.**\n\nReporting them separately stops one axis from masking the other.\n\n\nARGUMENTS: Review uncommitted working-tree changes against HEAD (1a5a02d..working tree, excluding notes/usage-ledger.csv and docs/transcripts/). Ticket: #13 (T11: Chart images on Reports), spec #11."}]},"isMeta":true,"turnCompanion":true,"uuid":"c94a5dcf-41da-4036-a6bb-527dcf83cf0e","timestamp":"2026-09-29T18:13:11.084Z","sourceToolUseID":"toolu_011hZUKdNUfP12L1q9LgFwmz","session_id":"fc138a42-1eee-4017-bff2-c6a77302f820","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/davelleat/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"60601091-56d6-4fd4-8e11-800778552d46","version":"2.1.284","gitBranch":"main"}

The user can send it another message and resume it, so the same task-id may notify more than once.</note>\n<result>**Spec review of T11 (#13, parent #11): the diff meets the spec.** I found no missing requirements and nothing implemented wrongly. There are three minor points below. `tests/test_t11_report_chart_images.py` passes (23 tests). The full suite has 14 failures, all in `test_ctx_guard.py` and `test_usage_report.py`, which have nothing to do with this diff.\n\n**(a) Missing or partial**\n\n1. **One guard has no test.** Spec: *\"Enforced server-side on every image route\"*, and the ticket's *\"Tests cover all of the above.\"* Every route checks `_editable_or_403` before it calls `reports.add_image` or `reports.remove_image`. So the check that matters in a race (the `drafts_only` UPDATE in `ContentTable.touch`) is never reached by any test, and the routes' `except reports.ReportLocked` branches are dead code in tests. If you removed `drafts_only=not is_director(user)` from both functions, every test would still pass. The behaviour itself is correct (see c). A test that goes through the client can't easily reach that branch. Either accept the gap or add one targeted test.\n2. **Upload validation is only partly re-tested for Reports.** Spec: *\"an SVG, an HTML file renamed .png, a truncated PNG, a mismatched extension or MIME type, a file over 5 MB, and an 11th image are each rejected.\"* T11 re-tests the SVG, the renamed HTML file, the empty upload and the 11th image. It leaves truncated, mismatched and oversized files to T10's tests. That is reasonable, since the code is shared and unchanged, and the test file's docstring says so.\n\n**(b) Not asked for (scope creep)**\n\n1. **T10's shared code was changed.** Ticket: *\"reusing T10's code unchanged.\"* `app/content.py` `ContentTable.touch` gained a `drafts_only` parameter. It defaults to off, so Data Bites behave exactly as before, and the lockdown needs it. Still, it modifies T10 code, and the commit message should say so.\n2. **A T04 error message changed.** Refactoring into `_editable_or_403` changed the 403 text on `edit_report` from \"Only the Director can edit a published Report.\" to \"…can change a published Report.\" It's harmless, since no test checks the old text, but it's outside the ticket.\n3. The `create()` step that clears images left under a reused id copies what T10 does for Data Bites. It fits the spirit of the ticket, so I don't count it as creep.\n\n**(c) Implemented, but possibly wrong**\n\nNothing blocking. Points I checked:\n- **Races:** the status check and the write are atomic. `touch` runs `UPDATE … WHERE id=? AND (status='draft' OR NOT ?)`, and `also` writes the image inside the same transaction, which holds SQLite's write lock. A concurrent publish therefore can't slip in between the check and the write. The only leftover risk is small: the image file is written before the commit, so if the commit itself failed, the file would stay on disk.\n- **Draft gate:** the public route goes through `get_published`, and `render_site` wipes `site/` before writing it. That meets *\"Unpublishing takes it down, and the next cms publish removes it from site/,\"* and tests cover it.\n- **Image and PDF independence:** they are stored and deleted separately, and tests cover both directions.\n- **Deleting a Report** removes its images (`remove_all`), and a test covers it.\n- **`image:&lt;name&gt;`** renders on the preview, the locked admin view, the public page and the export, with relative `src`. Tests cover each.\n- **Login and CSRF:** the router requires login on every route, and every POST requires CSRF. Tests cover both.</result>\n<usage><subagent_tokens>66363</subagent_tokens><tool_uses>7</tool_uses><duration_ms>125325</duration_ms></usage>\n</task-notification>"}

Relative paths, published-only reads, CSRF on every POST, sanitized Markdown, CONTEXT.md vocabulary, and prefixed CSS classes all check out. The judgement calls:\n\n| # | Finding | Resolution |\n|---|---|---|\n| 1 | Duplicated Code: the locked-Report message was written twice, as `_LOCKED` in `routes/reports.py` and inside `reports._missing_or_locked`. | **Fixed.** There is now one constant, `reports.LOCKED`, and both places use it. |\n| 2 | Duplicated Code / Shotgun Surgery: `report_image`, the `files()` comprehension, the public image route, and `_image_src` / `preview` / `serve_image` / `upload_image` mirror their Data Bite siblings. | **Kept.** There are two instances, and T10 set this shape on purpose, with the item modules owning permissions. If a third content type ever arrives, the shared helper can be extracted then. |\n| 3 | `drafts_only=not is_director(user)` appears three times in `reports.py`. | **Kept.** Each call site reads plainly and they match `update`. A helper would hide the rule rather than state it. |\n| 4 | Mysterious Name: the inner function `start` in `reports.create`. | **Fixed.** Renamed to `clear_images_then_attach`. |\n| 5 | The route pre-check and the `except ReportLocked` look redundant. | **Fixed.** The `_editable_or_403` docstring now explains the two layers: permission is checked before validation, and the atomic UPDATE guards against a publish that lands in between. |\n\n### Spec (#13, #11)\n\nNothing is missing and nothing is implemented wrongly. The points raised:\n\n| # | Finding | Resolution |\n|---|---|---|\n| a1 | No test reached the atomic `drafts_only` guard, because the route pre-check always rejected the request first. | **Fixed.** Added `test_a_report_published_after_the_page_checked_still_rejects_an_analyst`, which stubs the route's pre-check to simulate a publish that races it. I confirmed the test fails when the guard is removed. |\n| a2 | Upload validation is only partly re-tested for Reports. | **Accepted.** It is T10's shared, unchanged code (`chart_images.read`), already fully tested there. T11 spot-checks it: SVG, HTML renamed `.png`, no file, an 11th image. |\n| b1 | `ContentTable.touch` gained `drafts_only`, although the ticket says to reuse T10's code unchanged. | **Accepted and noted in the commit.** `chart_images` is untouched. `touch` needed the same draft guard that `update` already has, and it defaults to off, so Data Bites behave as before. |\n| b2 | The 403 text on `edit_report` changed from \"…edit a published Report.\" to \"…change a published Report.\" | **Accepted.** It now uses the single `reports.LOCKED` message that `ReportLocked` already used. No UI or test depends on the old text. |\n| c | Residual risk: the image is written before the commit, so a failed commit would leave the file on disk. | **Accepted.** T05 (the PDF) and T10 (Data Bite images) use the same pattern. `stored()` lists only files under a valid name, and a failed commit on an existing Report leaves at worst an image the item owns anyway. |\n\n**Tests:** `tests/test_t11_report_chart_images.py` has 24 tests, all passing. The full CMS suite passes. {"parentUuid":"a554d429-375d-44f5-8be8-1609000b1367","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011CfYBzR3ri8CkePNYpVNCU","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"T11 (#13, chart images on Reports) is done and committed locally as `e0b78f6`. I haven't pushed it, so #13 won't close until you do.\n\n**What it does**\n- **Lockdown:** Reports now take chart images using T10's `app/chart_images.py` unchanged. An Analyst can add or delete images on any draft Report; on a published Report only the Director can. An Analyst's attempt on a published Report gets a 403 before the upload is even read.\n- **Race case:** the lockdown is checked a second time inside the database write, so a Report published between the page's check and the write still rejects the Analyst.\n- **Public site and export:** images appear at `images/reports/<slug>/<name>` on the Report's page and in the `cms publish` output, with relative paths. Draft Reports' images are never served or exported, and unpublishing takes them down.\n- **Separate from the PDF:** a Report's images and its attached PDF are stored apart, and changing one leaves the other alone. Deleting a Report deletes both.\n- **Admin pages:** the edit page lists the images with a snippet to copy and shows them in the live preview. When a Report is locked to an Analyst, their read-only view still shows the images.\n\n**Tests:** all 24 tests in `tests/test_t11_report_chart_images.py` pass, and so does the rest of the CMS suite. There are 14 failures, all in `test_ctx_guard.py` and `test_usage_report.py` (the usage-tooling stubs that raise `NotImplementedError`). They fail the same way without my changes. {"parentUuid":"8a203457-2f75-4a40-80c1-73fcd1691aa1","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011CfYCQVRhgQA3LZpDd1YVv","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The site is already running on your machine, and it has the new image features.\n\n- **Public site:** http://localhost:8001/ shows what visitors will see: published Data Bites and Reports, with their chart images.\n- **Admin console:** http://localhost:8001/admin sends you to the login page. You upload images on a Data Bite's or Report's edit page, then paste the `![Description](image:<name>)` snippet into the body.\n\nIt's the `cms serve` you started earlier today on port 8001. It reloads itself when code changes, and it's already serving the new Report image pages.\n\n**It isn't on the internet yet.** GitHub Pages isn't turned on for the repo, so there's no public URL. To put it online:\n\n1. `uv run cms publish` writes the published content into `site/`.\n2. `uv run cms deploy` pushes `site/` to the `gh-pages` branch.\n3. On GitHub, go to repo **Settings → Pages → Deploy from a branch** and pick `gh-pages` and `/ (root)`.\n4. {"parentUuid":"e3029255-e37c-417a-ac93-a29bf6a12574","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"bb8292ca-7305-46ee-bdae-1fa3ddd59d36","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01MHtgBxxCxAyb9WJowKnmn8","type":"tool_result","content":"# MP2 Setup Exercise — Context-Threshold Warning Hook\n\n**Course:** IPHS 400 Frontiers of AI, Kenyon College, Fall 2026 (Jon Chun)\n**Where this goes:** Student manual, Part 1 (setup), right after the template repo is cloned and `/setup-matt-pocock-skills` has run.\n**Time:** 20–30 minutes. **Token cost:** under 3% of a 5-hour window (the scripts cost nothing at runtime; hooks run outside the model).\n**Rubric link:** Factor B, item B6 \"session hygiene\" (3 pts). The judge checks that the hook works and reads `docs/process/compaction-log.md`.\n**Verified against:** Claude Code hooks and status-line docs as of 2026-09-22. Record your own version with `claude --version` in `notes/setup_check.md`.\n\n---\n\n## Why you are building this\n\nPocock's loop runs one ticket per fresh context: `/clear`, then `/implement #N`. Most tickets finish well inside one window. A long ticket does not, and a model working in a very full context forgets the ticket's acceptance criteria and starts to drift from the spec. The course rule is:\n\n- **Short ticket:** `/clear` before it. Nothing else.\n- **Long ticket:** once context passes **50–60%**, `/compact` at the next **green test** (the end of a `/tdd` red-green-refactor cycle), never in the middle of a failing test, and always with a focus note.\n\nYou cannot follow that rule if you cannot see the number. This exercise gives you a live meter and a warning that fires at the right moment.\n\n## How it works\n\n```mermaid\nflowchart LR\n    CC[\"Claude Code session\"] -- \"session JSON on stdin<br/>(every refresh)\" --> SL[\"ctx_statusline.py<br/>prints: [Opus] ctx 47% ▓▓▓▓▓░░░░░\"]\n    SL -- \"writes\" --> ST[\".claude/state/ctx_&lt;session&gt;.json<br/>{pct: 47.2}\"]\n    CC -- \"Stop event<br/>(end of every Claude turn)\" --> G[\"ctx_guard.py\"]\n    ST -- \"reads\" --> G\n    G -- \"first time over 50 / 60 / 80%\" --> W[\"⚠ systemMessage shown to YOU\"]\n    CC -- \"PreCompact event\" --> L[\"ctx_compact_log.py\"]\n    L -- \"appends\" --> LOG[\"docs/process/compaction-log.md<br/>(grading evidence)\"]\n```\n\nThree facts from the Claude Code docs make this design work:\n\n1. **The status line already receives the context percentage** as `context_window.used_percentage` on stdin. The status line is the customizable bar under your prompt.\n2. **A `Stop` hook fires every time Claude finishes a turn.** The end of a turn is where a natural boundary (a green test) happens, so that is when the warning should appear.\n3. **A hook's `systemMessage` is shown to the user, not to Claude.** The warning talks to you, and does not pollute Claude's context.\n\nA hook cannot type `/compact` for you. Slash commands are yours. The hook only warns; you decide.\n\nEach herdr pane or terminal tab running Claude has its own `session_id`, so parallel sessions keep separate meters and never trip each other's warnings.\n\n## The four files\n\n| File | Job | Runs when |\n|---|---|---|\n| `.claude/hooks/ctx_statusline.py` | Shows the meter; records the percentage | Every status-line refresh |\n| `.claude/hooks/ctx_guard.py` | Warns at 50 / 60 / 80% | End of every Claude turn (`Stop`) |\n| `.claude/hooks/ctx_compact_log.py` | Logs each compaction and its focus note | Before every compaction (`PreCompact`) |\n| `tests/test_ctx_guard.py` | Proves the logic works | When `/tdd` or `/code-review` runs the suite |\n\n---\n\n## Step 1 — Check Python\n\nIn Ghostty (macOS) or Windows Terminal (WSL2), inside your `iphs400-mp2-cms` folder:\n\n```bash\npython3 --version\n```\n\n**Expected:** `Python 3.9` or newer (the `uv` setup from the setup manual gives you 3.12).\n**If you see `command not found`:** macOS runs `xcode-select --install`; WSL2 runs `sudo apt install -y python3`. Then retry.\n\n## Step 2 — Open the hook files\n\nThe template already contains all four files. Open the folder in VS Code:\n\n```bash\ncode .\n```\n\nIn the Explorer panel, expand `.claude/hooks/`. You should see `ctx_statusline.py`, `ctx_guard.py`, and `ctx_compact_log.py`.\n\n**If `.claude` is not visible:** VS Code hides nothing by default, but macOS Finder hides dot-folders. Use VS Code, or run `ls -la .claude/hooks` in the terminal.\n\n## Step 3 — Read the status-line script\n\nThis file is complete. Read it so you know what it does; you will explain it in your report.\n\n```python\n#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"Status line for IPHS 400 MP2.\n\nClaude Code runs this script on every status-line refresh and pipes session\nJSON to stdin. The script does two things:\n  1. prints one line under the prompt:  [Opus] ctx 47% ▓▓▓▓▓░░░░░\n  2. records the context percentage in .claude/state/ctx_<session>.json so the\n     Stop hook (ctx_guard.py) can read it at the end of each turn.\nIt must never crash: a broken status line hides the meter, nothing else.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport json\nimport os\nimport sys\nimport time\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\n\ndef project_dir(data: dict) -> Path:\n    ws = data.get(\"workspace\") or {}\n    return Path(\n        os.environ.get(\"CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR\")\n        or ws.get(\"project_dir\")\n        or ws.get(\"current_dir\")\n        or os.getcwd()\n    )\n\n\ndef bar(pct: float, width: int = 10) -> str:\n    filled = max(0, min(width, round(pct / 100 * width)))\n    return \"▓\" * filled + \"░\" * (width - filled)\n\n\ndef main() -> None:\n    try:\n        data = json.load(sys.stdin)\n    except Exception:\n        print(\"ctx ?\")\n        return\n\n    model = (data.get(\"model\") or {}).get(\"display_name\", \"Claude\")\n    pct = (data.get(\"context_window\") or {}).get(\"used_percentage\")\n    if pct is None:\n        print(f\"[{model}] ctx --\")\n        return\n    pct = float(pct)\n\n    session = data.get(\"session_id\") or \"default\"\n    state_dir = project_dir(data) / \".claude\" / \"state\"\n    try:\n        state_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n        tmp = state_dir / f\"ctx_{session}.json.tmp\"\n        tmp.write_text(json.dumps({\"pct\": pct, \"ts\": time.time()}))\n        tmp.replace(state_dir / f\"ctx_{session}.json\")  # atomic swap\n    except OSError:\n        pass  # meter still prints even if the disk write fails\n\n    flag = \"  ⚠ compact at next green test\" if pct >= 60 else \"\"\n    print(f\"[{model}] ctx {pct:.0f}% {bar(pct)}{flag}\")\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    main()\n```\n\n## Step 4 — Write the Stop hook's logic (the exercise)\n\nThe template ships `ctx_guard.py` with everything written **except the body of `decide()`**, which raises `NotImplementedError`. Seven of the ten tests in `tests/test_ctx_guard.py` fail until you finish it. This is your first practice run of the loop on something tiny.\n\nIn a fresh Claude Code session:\n\n```text\n/clear\n/tdd Implement decide() in .claude/hooks/ctx_guard.py so the failing tests in tests/test_ctx_guard.py pass. Do not change the tests or any other function.\n```\n\n`/tdd` runs the tests, watches them fail, writes the code, and runs them again until they pass. You do not type `pytest` yourself.\n\nThe rules `decide()` must follow:\n\n- Map the percentage to a band: 0 = below 50, 1 = 50+, 2 = 60+, 3 = 80+ (the thresholds come from `thresholds()`).\n- **Warn once per upward crossing.** Going from 52% to 55% must stay quiet.\n- **Re-arm after compaction.** When usage drops (after `/compact` or `/clear`), remember the lower band so the next crossing warns again.\n\nWhen the tests pass, compare your version with the complete file below.\n\n\n## Step 5 — Read the compaction logger\n\nThis file is complete. It writes the evidence the judge reads for rubric item B6.\n\n```python\n#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"PreCompact hook: log every compaction to docs/process/compaction-log.md.\n\nThis is grading evidence for rubric item B6 (session hygiene):\n  - trigger \"manual\" + a focus note  = you compacted on purpose (good)\n  - trigger \"auto\"                   = the session overflowed (fix the habit)\nNever exits 2: exit 2 on PreCompact would BLOCK compaction.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport json\nimport os\nimport sys\nfrom datetime import datetime, timezone\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nHEADER = (\n    \"# Compaction log\\n\\n\"\n    \"| UTC time | Session | Trigger | Focus note |\\n\"\n    \"|---|---|---|---|\\n\"\n)\n\n\ndef main() -> None:\n    try:\n        event = json.load(sys.stdin)\n    except Exception:\n        return\n    project = Path(os.environ.get(\"CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR\") or event.get(\"cwd\") or os.getcwd())\n    log = project / \"docs\" / \"process\" / \"compaction-log.md\"\n    log.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n    if not log.exists():\n        log.write_text(HEADER)\n    note = (event.get(\"custom_instructions\") or \"\").replace(\"|\", \"/\").replace(\"\\n\", \" \").strip()\n    row = \"| {} | {} | {} | {} |\\n\".format(\n        datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime(\"%Y-%m-%d %H:%M\"),\n        (event.get(\"session_id\") or \"?\")[:8],\n        event.get(\"trigger\", \"unknown\"),\n        note or \"(none)\",\n    )\n    with log.open(\"a\") as f:\n        f.write(row)\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    try:\n        main()\n    except Exception:\n        pass\n    sys.exit(0)\n```\n\n**Warning:** never change its exit code to 2. On `PreCompact`, exit code 2 **blocks compaction**, which would lock you inside an overflowing session.\n\n## Step 6 — Confirm the hooks are registered\n\nThe template already registers all three in `.claude/settings.json`, together with\nthe `SessionEnd` transcript saver. Read that file now so you know what is wired up:\n\n```bash\ncat .claude/settings.json\n```\n\n**Expected:** a `statusLine` entry plus `Stop`, `PreCompact`, and `SessionEnd`\nhooks, each pointing at a script in `.claude/hooks/`. Check it is valid JSON:\n\n```bash\npython3 -m json.tool .claude/settings.json > /dev/null && echo \"settings OK\"\n```\n\n**Expected:** `settings OK`. If you ever edit this file and see\n`Expecting ',' delimiter`, a comma is missing at the line number shown.\n\n## Step 7 — Keep the state files out of git\n\nThe meter's scratch files are per-session and per-laptop. They must not be committed:\n\n```bash\ngrep -qxF '.claude/state/' .gitignore || echo '.claude/state/' >> .gitignore\ntail -3 .gitignore\n```\n\n**Expected:** `.claude/state/` appears in the last lines. (`docs/process/compaction-log.md` *is* committed; it is evidence.)\n\n## Step 8 — Test the scripts without Claude\n\nPipe fake session data in, exactly as Claude Code would:\n\n```bash\nexport CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR=\"$PWD\"\n\necho '{\"session_id\":\"demo\",\"model\":{\"display_name\":\"Opus\"},\"context_window\":{\"used_percentage\":63}}' \\\n  | python3 .claude/hooks/ctx_statusline.py\n\necho '{\"session_id\":\"demo\",\"hook_event_name\":\"Stop\"}' | python3 .claude/hooks/ctx_guard.py\necho '{\"session_id\":\"demo\",\"hook_event_name\":\"Stop\"}' | python3 .claude/hooks/ctx_guard.py\n\nrm -f .claude/state/ctx_demo*.json\n```\n\n**Expected output, in order:**\n\n1. `[Opus] ctx 63% ▓▓▓▓▓▓░░░░  ⚠ compact at next green test`\n2. `{\"systemMessage\": \"Context 63%: at the next green test run  /compact keep: ticket #N acceptance criteria, what is left, files touched\"}`\n3. *(nothing)*: the second call is silent because it already warned once.\n\n## Step 9 — Test it live with low thresholds\n\nStart Claude with thresholds so low that the first reply trips them:\n\n```bash\nCTX_WARN_PCT=1 CTX_COMPACT_PCT=2 claude\n```\n\n1. Look under the prompt. **Expected:** `[<model>] ctx N% ▓░░░░░░░░░`.\n2. Type `/hooks`. **Expected:** `Stop` and `PreCompact` each show 1+ hooks with the source `Project Settings`. Press Esc.\n3. Type `say hi`. After Claude answers, **expected:** a warning line starting `Context N%:`.\n4. Type `/compact keep: hook test`. Then open `docs/process/compaction-log.md`. **Expected:** a new row ending `| manual | keep: hook test |`.\n5. Type `/exit`. From now on start Claude normally (`claude`), and the real 50/60/80% thresholds apply.\n\nDelete the test row from `docs/process/compaction-log.md` so your log starts clean.\n\n## Step 10 — Commit\n\n```text\nCommit the context-threshold hooks, settings.json, .gitignore, and tests/test_ctx_guard.py with the message \"setup: context-threshold warning hook\" and push.\n```\n\nCheck on GitHub that the commit appears, and that `.claude/state/` is **not** in the repo.\n\n---\n\n## Using it during tickets\n\n| You see | Do this |\n|---|---|\n| Meter under 50% | Keep working. |\n| `Context 5x%: … plan a /compact` | Let the current red-green cycle finish. |\n| `Context 6x%: at the next green test run /compact keep: …` | As soon as the tests are green, type `/compact keep: ticket #N acceptance criteria, what is left, files touched` (with the real ticket number). |\n| `Context 8x%: compact now …` | Compact immediately, or `/handoff` and start a new session. Afterward, ask whether the ticket should be split with `/to-tickets`. |\n| A log row with trigger `auto` | The session overflowed and Claude compacted on its own. It is not an error, but the judge counts it against B6; next time, compact yourself at 60%. |\n| Starting the next short ticket | `/clear`. No compaction needed. |\n\n## Troubleshooting\n\n| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |\n|---|---|---|\n| No meter under the prompt | `statusLine` block missing, or JSON invalid | Rerun the Step 6 JSON check; restart Claude |\n| Meter shows `ctx --` | Your Claude Code version does not send `context_window` | Run `claude update`, restart |\n| Meter works, never any warning | Stop hook not registered, or the path is wrong | `/hooks` should list it; if it shows `Failed with non-blocking status code`, the path in `settings.json` is wrong |\n| `python3: command not found` inside the hook | Hook shell has a different PATH | Replace `python3` in `settings.json` with the full path from `which python3` |\n| Compaction log never appears | `PreCompact` entry missing | Recheck Step 6 with `/hooks` |\n| Focus note column says `(none)` | You ran `/compact` with no note, or your version names the field differently | Always type a note; if it still shows `(none)`, tell the instructor your `claude --version` |\n| Warnings pop up in the wrong pane | Should not happen: each session has its own state file | Delete `.claude/state/` and restart both sessions |\n\nIf none of these fix it, follow the self-help ladder in the manual: reread the error, run `/hooks`, ask Claude to explain the error before changing anything, check the [hooks reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks) and [status line docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/statusline), log it with `/teach-log`, then email the instructor with the error pasted in.\n\n## Saved? ✓\n\nBefore moving on, all of these must be true:\n\n- [ ] `.claude/hooks/ctx_statusline.py`, `ctx_guard.py`, `ctx_compact_log.py` committed\n- [ ] `.claude/settings.json` contains `statusLine`, `Stop`, and `PreCompact` entries, and passes the JSON check\n- [ ] `tests/test_ctx_guard.py` committed, and `/tdd` reported all 10 tests passing\n- [ ] `.claude/state/` listed in `.gitignore` and absent from GitHub\n- [ ] `claude --version` recorded in `notes/setup_check.md`\n\n## Complete test file (template contents)\n\n```python\n\"\"\"Tests for the context-threshold hooks (IPHS 400 MP2, setup exercise).\"\"\"\nimport importlib.util\nimport json\nimport os\nimport subprocess\nimport sys\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nHOOKS = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / \".claude\" / \"hooks\"\n\n\ndef load(name):\n    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(name, HOOKS / f\"{name}.py\")\n    mod = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)\n    spec.loader.exec_module(mod)\n    return mod\n\n\nguard = load(\"ctx_guard\")\n\n\ndef run(script, payload, project, **env):\n    return subprocess.run(\n        [sys.executable, str(HOOKS / script)],\n        input=json.dumps(payload),\n        capture_output=True,\n        text=True,\n        env={**os.environ, \"CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR\": str(project), **env},\n    )\n\n\n# ---- pure logic -----------------------------------------------------------\n\ndef test_silent_below_50():\n    assert guard.decide(49.9, guard.NONE) == (None, guard.NONE)\n\n\ndef test_warns_once_at_50():\n    msg, band = guard.decide(52, guard.NONE)\n    assert band == guard.WARN and \"52%\" in msg\n    assert guard.decide(55, band) == (None, guard.WARN)  # no nagging\n\n\ndef test_compact_message_at_60_names_focus_note():\n    msg, band = guard.decide(61, guard.WARN)\n    assert band == guard.COMPACT and \"/compact keep:\" in msg\n\n\ndef Hook\n\n**Course:** IPHS 400 Frontiers of AI, Kenyon College, Fall 2026 (Jon Chun)\n**Where this goes:** Student manual, Part 1 (setup), right after the template repo is cloned and `/setup-matt-pocock-skills` has run.\n**Time:** 20–30 minutes. **Token cost:** under 3% of a 5-hour window (the scripts cost nothing at runtime; hooks run outside the model).\n**Rubric link:** Factor B, item B6 \"session hygiene\" (3 pts). The judge checks that the hook works and reads `docs/process/compaction-log.md`.\n**Verified against:** Claude Code hooks and status-line docs as of 2026-09-22. Record your own version with `claude --version` in `notes/setup_check.md`.\n\n---\n\n## Why you are building this\n\nPocock's loop runs one ticket per fresh context: `/clear`, then `/implement #N`. Most tickets finish well inside one window. A long ticket does not, and a model working in a very full context forgets the ticket's acceptance criteria and starts to drift from the spec. The course rule is:\n\n- **Short ticket:** `/clear` before it. Nothing else.\n- **Long ticket:** once context passes **50–60%**, `/compact` at the next **green test** (the end of a `/tdd` red-green-refactor cycle), never in the middle of a failing test, and always with a focus note.\n\nYou cannot follow that rule if you cannot see the number. This exercise gives you a live meter and a warning that fires at the right moment.\n\n## How it works\n\n```mermaid\nflowchart LR\n    CC[\"Claude Code session\"] -- \"session JSON on stdin<br/>(every refresh)\" --> SL[\"ctx_statusline.py<br/>prints: [Opus] ctx 47% ▓▓▓▓▓░░░░░\"]\n    SL -- \"writes\" --> ST[\".claude/state/ctx_&lt;session&gt;.json<br/>{pct: 47.2}\"]\n    CC -- \"Stop event<br/>(end of every Claude turn)\" --> G[\"ctx_guard.py\"]\n    ST -- \"reads\" --> G\n    G -- \"first time over 50 / 60 / 80%\" --> W[\"⚠ systemMessage shown to YOU\"]\n    CC -- \"PreCompact event\" --> L[\"ctx_compact_log.py\"]\n    L -- \"appends\" --> LOG[\"docs/process/compaction-log.md<br/>(grading evidence)\"]\n```\n\nThree facts from the Claude Code docs make this design work:\n\n1. **The status line already receives the context percentage** as `context_window.used_percentage` on stdin. The status line is the customizable bar under your prompt.\n2. **A `Stop` hook fires every time Claude finishes a turn.** The end of a turn is where a natural boundary (a green test) happens, so that is when the warning should appear.\n3. **A hook's `systemMessage` is shown to the user, not to Claude.** The warning talks to you, and does not pollute Claude's context.\n\nA hook cannot type `/compact` for you. Slash commands are yours. The hook only warns; you decide.\n\nEach herdr pane or terminal tab running Claude has its own `session_id`, so parallel sessions keep separate meters and never trip each other's warnings.\n\n## The four files\n\n| File | Job | Runs when |\n|---|---|---|\n| `.claude/hooks/ctx_statusline.py` | Shows the meter; records the percentage | Every status-line refresh |\n| `.claude/hooks/ctx_guard.py` | Warns at 50 / 60 / 80% | End of every Claude turn (`Stop`) |\n| `.claude/hooks/ctx_compact_log.py` | Logs each compaction and its focus note | Before every compaction (`PreCompact`) |\n| `tests/test_ctx_guard.py` | Proves the logic works | When `/tdd` or `/code-review` runs the suite |\n\n---\n\n## Step 1 — Check Python\n\nIn Ghostty (macOS) or Windows Terminal (WSL2), inside your `iphs400-mp2-cms` folder:\n\n```bash\npython3 --version\n```\n\n**Expected:** `Python 3.9` or newer (the `uv` setup from the setup manual gives you 3.12).\n**If you see `command not found`:** macOS runs `xcode-select --install`; WSL2 runs `sudo apt install -y python3`. Then retry.\n\n## Step 2 — Open the hook files\n\nThe template already contains all four files. Open the folder in VS Code:\n\n```bash\ncode .\n```\n\nIn the Explorer panel, expand `.claude/hooks/`. You should see `ctx_statusline.py`, `ctx_guard.py`, and `ctx_compact_log.py`.\n\n**If `.claude` is not visible:** VS Code hides nothing by default, but macOS Finder hides dot-folders. Use VS Code, or run `ls -la .claude/hooks` in the terminal.\n\n## Step 3 — Read the status-line script\n\nThis file is complete. Read it so you know what it does; you will explain it in your report.\n\n```python\n#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"Status line for IPHS 400 MP2.\n\nClaude Code runs this script on every status-line refresh and pipes session\nJSON to stdin. The script does two things:\n  1. prints one line under the prompt:  [Opus] ctx 47% ▓▓▓▓▓░░░░░\n  2. records the context percentage in .claude/state/ctx_<session>.json so the\n     Stop hook (ctx_guard.py) can read it at the end of each turn.\nIt must never crash: a broken status line hides the meter, nothing else.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport json\nimport os\nimport sys\nimport time\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\n\ndef project_dir(data: dict) -> Path:\n    ws = data.get(\"workspace\") or {}\n    return Path(\n        os.environ.get(\"CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR\")\n        or ws.get(\"project_dir\")\n        or ws.get(\"current_dir\")\n        or os.getcwd()\n    )\n\n\ndef bar(pct: float, width: int = 10) -> str:\n    filled = max(0, min(width, round(pct / 100 * width)))\n    return \"▓\" * filled + \"░\" * (width - filled)\n\n\ndef main() -> None:\n    try:\n        data = json.load(sys.stdin)\n    except Exception:\n        print(\"ctx ?\")\n        return\n\n    model = (data.get(\"model\") or {}).get(\"display_name\", \"Claude\")\n    pct = (data.get(\"context_window\") or {}).get(\"used_percentage\")\n    if pct is None:\n        print(f\"[{model}] ctx --\")\n        return\n    pct = float(pct)\n\n    session = data.get(\"session_id\") or \"default\"\n    state_dir = project_dir(data) / \".claude\" / \"state\"\n    try:\n        state_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n        tmp = state_dir / f\"ctx_{session}.json.tmp\"\n        tmp.write_text(json.dumps({\"pct\": pct, \"ts\": time.time()}))\n        tmp.replace(state_dir / f\"ctx_{session}.json\")  # atomic swap\n    except OSError:\n        pass  # meter still prints even if the disk write fails\n\n    flag = \"  ⚠ compact at next green test\" if pct >= 60 else \"\"\n    print(f\"[{model}] ctx {pct:.0f}% {bar(pct)}{flag}\")\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    main()\n```\n\n## Step 4 — Write the Stop hook's logic (the exercise)\n\nThe template ships `ctx_guard.py` with everything written **except the body of `decide()`**, which raises `NotImplementedError`. Seven of the ten tests in `tests/test_ctx_guard.py` fail until you finish it. This is your first practice run of the loop on something tiny.\n\nIn a fresh Claude Code session:\n\n```text\n/clear\n/tdd Implement decide() in .claude/hooks/ctx_guard.py so the failing tests in tests/test_ctx_guard.py pass. Do not change the tests or any other function.\n```\n\n`/tdd` runs the tests, watches them fail, writes the code, and runs them again until they pass. You do not type `pytest` yourself.\n\nThe rules `decide()` must follow:\n\n- Map the percentage to a band: 0 = below 50, 1 = 50+, 2 = 60+, 3 = 80+ (the thresholds come from `thresholds()`).\n- **Warn once per upward crossing.** Going from 52% to 55% must stay quiet.\n- **Re-arm after compaction.** When usage drops (after `/compact` or `/clear`), remember the lower band so the next crossing warns again.\n\nWhen the tests pass, compare your version with the complete file below.\n\n\n## Step 5 — Read the compaction logger\n\nThis file is complete. It writes the evidence the judge reads for rubric item B6.\n\n```python\n#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"PreCompact hook: log every compaction to docs/process/compaction-log.md.\n\nThis is grading evidence for rubric item B6 (session hygiene):\n  - trigger \"manual\" + a focus note  = you compacted on purpose (good)\n  - trigger \"auto\"                   = the session overflowed (fix the habit)\nNever exits 2: exit 2 on PreCompact would BLOCK compaction.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport json\nimport os\nimport sys\nfrom datetime import datetime, timezone\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nHEADER = (\n    \"# Compaction log\\n\\n\"\n    \"| UTC time | Session | Trigger | Focus note |\\n\"\n    \"|---|---|---|---|\\n\"\n)\n\n\ndef main() -> None:\n    try:\n        event = json.load(sys.stdin)\n    except Exception:\n        return\n    project = Path(os.environ.get(\"CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR\") or event.get(\"cwd\") or os.getcwd())\n    log = project / \"docs\" / \"process\" / \"compaction-log.md\"\n    log.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n    if not log.exists():\n        log.write_text(HEADER)\n    note = (event.get(\"custom_instructions\") or \"\").replace(\"|\", \"/\").replace(\"\\n\", \" \").strip()\n    row = \"| {} | {} | {} | {} |\\n\".format(\n        datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime(\"%Y-%m-%d %H:%M\"),\n        (event.get(\"session_id\") or \"?\")[:8],\n        event.get(\"trigger\", \"unknown\"),\n        note or \"(none)\",\n    )\n    with log.open(\"a\") as f:\n        f.write(row)\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    try:\n        main()\n    except Exception:\n        pass\n    sys.exit(0)\n```\n\n**Warning:** never change its exit code to 2. On `PreCompact`, exit code 2 **blocks compaction**, which would lock you inside an overflowing session.\n\n## Step 6 — Confirm the hooks are registered\n\nThe template already registers all three in `.claude/settings.json`, together with\nthe `SessionEnd` transcript saver. Read that file now so you know what is wired up:\n\n```bash\ncat .claude/settings.json\n```\n\n**Expected:** a `statusLine` entry plus `Stop`, `PreCompact`, and `SessionEnd`\nhooks, each pointing at a script in `.claude/hooks/`. Check it is valid JSON:\n\n```bash\npython3 -m json.tool .claude/settings.json > /dev/null && echo \"settings OK\"\n```\n\n**Expected:** `settings OK`. If you ever edit this file and see\n`Expecting ',' delimiter`, a comma is missing at the line number shown.\n\n## Step 7 — Keep the state files out of git\n\nThe meter's scratch files are per-session and per-laptop. They must not be committed:\n\n```bash\ngrep -qxF '.claude/state/' .gitignore || echo '.claude/state/' >> .gitignore\ntail -3 .gitignore\n```\n\n**Expected:** `.claude/state/` appears in the last lines. (`docs/process/compaction-log.md` *is* committed; it is evidence.)\n\n## Step 8 — Test the scripts without Claude\n\nPipe fake session data in, exactly as Claude Code would:\n\n```bash\nexport CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR=\"$PWD\"\n\necho '{\"session_id\":\"demo\",\"model\":{\"display_name\":\"Opus\"},\"context_window\":{\"used_percentage\":63}}' \\\n  | python3 .claude/hooks/ctx_statusline.py\n\necho '{\"session_id\":\"demo\",\"hook_event_name\":\"Stop\"}' | python3 .claude/hooks/ctx_guard.py\necho '{\"session_id\":\"demo\",\"hook_event_name\":\"Stop\"}' | python3 .claude/hooks/ctx_guard.py\n\nrm -f .claude/state/ctx_demo*.json\n```\n\n**Expected output, in order:**\n\n1. `[Opus] ctx 63% ▓▓▓▓▓▓░░░░  ⚠ compact at next green test`\n2. `{\"systemMessage\": \"Context 63%: at the next green test run  /compact keep: ticket #N acceptance criteria, what is left, files touched\"}`\n3. *(nothing)*: the second call is silent because it already warned once.\n\n## Step 9 — Test it live with low thresholds\n\nStart Claude with thresholds so low that the first reply trips them:\n\n```bash\nCTX_WARN_PCT=1 CTX_COMPACT_PCT=2 claude\n```\n\n1. Look under the prompt. **Expected:** `[<model>] ctx N% ▓░░░░░░░░░`.\n2. Type `/hooks`. **Expected:** `Stop` and `PreCompact` each show 1+ hooks with the source `Project Settings`. Press Esc.\n3. It reads the percentage the status line recorded, and\nprints {\"systemMessage\": \"...\"} the first time usage crosses a threshold.\nThe message is shown to YOU, not to Claude. The hook never blocks and never\nruns /compact itself: slash commands are yours to type.\n\nThresholds (override when launching:  CTX_WARN_PCT=1 claude  to test):\n  CTX_WARN_PCT     default 50  -> \"plan a /compact\"\n  CTX_COMPACT_PCT  default 60  -> \"/compact at the next green test\"\n  urgent = CTX_COMPACT_PCT + 20 -> \"compact or /handoff now; consider splitting\"\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport csv\nimport json\nimport os\nimport sys\nfrom datetime import datetime, timezone\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nNONE, WARN, COMPACT, URGENT = 0, 1, 2, 3\n\n\ndef thresholds() -> tuple[float, float, float]:\n    warn = float(os.environ.get(\"CTX_WARN_PCT\", 50))\n    compact = float(os.environ.get(\"CTX_COMPACT_PCT\", 60))\n    return warn, compact, compact + 20\n\n\ndef band_for(pct: float, warn: float, compact: float, urgent: float) -> int:\n    if pct >= urgent:\n        return URGENT\n    if pct >= compact:\n        return COMPACT\n    if pct >= warn:\n        return WARN\n    return NONE\n\n\ndef message_for(band: int, pct: float) -> str:\n    p = f\"{pct:.0f}%\"\n    return {\n        WARN: (\n            f\"Context {p}: finish the current red-green cycle, then plan a \"\n            \"/compact at the next green test.\"\n        ),\n        COMPACT: (\n            f\"Context {p}: at the next green test run  /compact keep: ticket #N \"\n            \"acceptance criteria, what is left, files touched\"\n        ),\n        URGENT: (\n            f\"Context {p}: compact now (or /handoff and start fresh). If this \"\n            \"ticket keeps overflowing, split it with /to-tickets.\"\n        ),\n    }[band]\n\n\ndef decide(pct: float, last_band: int) -> tuple[str | None, int]:\n    \"\"\"Pure function (unit-tested): return (message or None, band to store).\n\n    Warn once per upward crossing. When usage drops (after /compact or\n    /clear), store the lower band so the next crossing warns again.\n    \"\"\"\n    raise NotImplementedError(\"MP2 Exercise A: implement me with /tdd\")\n\nLEDGER_COLUMNS = [\n    \"ts\", \"session\", \"phase\", \"provider\", \"model\", \"effort\",\n    \"ctx_pct\", \"five_h_pct\", \"weekly_pct\",\n]\n\n\ndef log_usage(project: Path, session: str, state: dict) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Append one row per turn to notes/usage-ledger.csv (rubric item B7).\"\"\"\n    ledger = project / \"notes\" / \"usage-ledger.csv\"\n    phase_file = project / \".claude\" / \"state\" / \"phase\"\n    try:\n        phase = phase_file.read_text().strip() or \"unlabelled\"\n    except OSError:\n        phase = \"unlabelled\"\n\n    def cell(value: object) -> str:\n        return \"\" if value is None else str(value)\n\n    row = [\n        datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime(\"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ\"),\n        session[:8], phase, cell(state.get(\"provider\")), cell(state.get(\"model\")),\n        cell(state.get(\"effort\")), f\"{float(state.get('pct', 0)):.1f}\",\n        cell(state.get(\"five_h\")), cell(state.get(\"weekly\")),\n    ]\n    try:\n        ledger.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n        new = not ledger.exists()\n        with ledger.open(\"a\", newline=\"\") as f:\n            writer = csv.writer(f)\n            if new:\n                writer.writerow(LEDGER_COLUMNS)\n            writer.writerow(row)\n    except OSError:\n        pass\n\n\ndef main() -> None:\n    try:\n        event = json.load(sys.stdin)\n    except Exception:\n        return\n    project = Path(os.environ.get(\"CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR\") or event.get(\"cwd\") or os.getcwd())\n    session = event.get(\"session_id\") or \"default\"\n    state_dir = project / \".claude\" / \"state\"\n    ctx_file = state_dir / f\"ctx_{session}.json\"\n    band_file = state_dir / f\"ctx_{session}_band.json\"\n\n    try:\n        state = json.loads(ctx_file.read_text())\n        pct = float(state[\"pct\"])\n    except (OSError, ValueError, KeyError):\n        return  # no status-line data yet: stay silent\n    try:\n        last_band = int(json.loads(band_file.read_text())[\"band\"])\n    except (OSError, ValueError, KeyError):\n        last_band = NONE\n\n    log_usage(project, session, state)\n\n    msg, band = decide(pct, last_band)\n    try:\n        band_file.write_text(json.dumps({\"band\": band}))\n    except OSError:\n        pass\n    if msg:\n        print(json.dumps({\"systemMessage\": msg}))\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    try:\n        main()\n    except Exception:\n        pass  # a warning hook must never break the session\n    sys.exit(0)\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":64,"oldLines":7,"newStart":64,"newLines":10,"lines":["     Warn once per upward crossing. {"parentUuid":"c01f9b6a-80f8-41ef-a5d9-1497683d779d","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"bb8292ca-7305-46ee-bdae-1fa3ddd59d36","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01A8EQDgf5BM7tqWLu6Y9Rpb","type":"tool_result","content":"#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"Turn notes/usage-ledger.csv into a plan-vs-actual budget report.\n\nUsage:\n    uv run python scripts/usage_report.py                 # summary + forecast\n    uv run python scripts/usage_report.py --remaining 4   # 4 tickets still to do\n\nWhy positive deltas: the 5-hour and weekly meters RESET (drop to 0) when their\nwindow rolls over, and the weekly one only ever climbs inside a week. Summing\nonly the increases between consecutive rows measures what you actually spent\nand ignores the resets. That is what spend() does, and it is your exercise.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport argparse\nimport csv\nfrom collections import defaultdict\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nLEDGER = Path(\"notes/usage-ledger.csv\")\n\n\ndef spend(series: list[float | None]) -> float:\n    \"\"\"Total rise across a meter that can reset to a lower value.\n\n    Sum every increase between consecutive readings; ignore blanks (None) and\n    any drop, which means the window reset.\n\n    >>> spend([10.0, 12.0, 15.0])\n    5.0\n    >>> spend([80.0, 5.0, 9.0])\n    4.0\n    >>> spend([None, 4.0, None, 7.0])\n    3.0\n    \"\"\"\n    raise NotImplementedError(\"MP2 Exercise B: implement me with /tdd\")\n\ndef read_rows(path: Path) -> list[dict]:\n    with path.open(newline=\"\") as f:\n        return list(csv.DictReader(f))\n\n\ndef to_float(text: str | None) -> float | None:\n    try:\n        return float(text) if text not in (None, \"\") else None\n    except ValueError:\n        return None\n\n\ndef by_phase(rows: list[dict]) -> dict[str, dict]:\n    phases: dict[str, dict] = defaultdict(\n        lambda: {\"turns\": 0, \"five\": [], \"weekly\": [], \"models\": set(), \"providers\": set()}\n    )\n    for row in rows:\n        phase = phases[row.get(\"phase\") or \"unlabelled\"]\n        phase[\"turns\"] += 1\n        phase[\"five\"].append(to_float(row.get(\"five_h_pct\")))\n        phase[\"weekly\"].append(to_float(row.get(\"weekly_pct\")))\n        if row.get(\"model\"):\n            phase[\"models\"].add(row[\"model\"])\n        if row.get(\"provider\"):\n            phase[\"providers\"].add(row[\"provider\"])\n    return phases\n\n\ndef ticket_phases(phases: dict[str, dict]) -> list[str]:\n    return sorted(p for p in phases if p.upper().startswith(\"T\") and p[1:].isdigit())\n\n\ndef main() -> None:\n    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()\n    ap.add_argument(\"--ledger\", type=Path, default=LEDGER)\n    ap.add_argument(\"--remaining\", type=int, default=0, help=\"tickets not yet built\")\n    args = ap.parse_args()\n\n    if not args.ledger.exists():\n        raise SystemExit(f\"No ledger at {args.ledger}.
